sorries.obstruction: l.1601-1604: that the regular part of a sub-spear of M2's spear at a BTZ point of M1 lies in M0. The printed route (Sigma_0 is a Cauchy surface of N := (M0 \ J+(C')) u reg(Int S \ J-_S(C'')) by 'a simple analysis using lem:intersect_number_complete', then N subset M0 by Cauchy-maximality) is not printed in detail; it applies lem:blunt_spear_neighborhood to Sigma_0 before reg(S) subset M0 is known (OQ-143 (e)); and the strict lem_surface_complete_two needs a C1 graph, which the Lipschitz reading of Cauchy-complete does not supply

l.1604 asserts 'M1 u Int(S1) is a globally hyperbolic BTZ-extension of M1' without proof; an open subset of the GH M2 need not be GH. Causal convexity of M1 u Int(S1) in M2 needs that the causal past of a BTZ point of Int(S1) is the part of the chart's axis below it (Causal.SingularFlatAxioms.Jminus_eq_image matched with the axis parametrization of S1's chart), not in the library

findings: BTZ_1.tex:1604 ('Notice M_1 u Int(S_1) is a globally hyperbolic BTZ-extension of M_1'): a missing justification, not an error. Global hyperbolicity is asserted without proof. An open subset of the globally hyperbolic M_2 is globally hyperbolic when it is causally convex, and causal convexity here needs the causal past of the BTZ points of Int(S_1) to stay on S_1's axis. Left as a tagged sorry.

BTZ_1.tex:1604 ('Therefore, every BTZ-line of M_1 admits a spear neighborhood'): Int(S_1) subset M_1 does not by itself give a spear of M_1, since the vertex p' of S_1 is on the boundary of Int(S_1). One shrinks to a spear of higher vertex and smaller radius inside Int(S_1), and checks it is around the same BTZ line of M_1 as p. That last point uses the causal convexity of M_1 in M_2, which the paper does not mention. Proved (exists_spearNbhd_of_subset, causallyConvexIn_range).

BTZ_1.tex:1601 (with OQ-143 (e), already recorded): lem:blunt_spear_neighborhood is applied to Sigma_0 in M_0 with the spear of M_2 from lem:tube before reg(S) subset M_0 is established (l.1604). Not formalized.

BTZ_1.tex:1600 vs l.1598, a harmless notational slip: the proof's 'Delta a BTZ-line of M_2' is a line of M_1 read in M_2. Every BTZ line of M_2 meets Sigma_1 (a Cauchy surface of M_1, hence of its Cauchy extension M_2), and M_1 is causally convex in M_2, so the BTZ lines of M_1 and M_2 correspond one to one.
questions: 'Cauchy-complete' for M_0 (l.1595): the Lipschitz form of DEC-31/35 (what prop_reg_complete proves for Reg M) or the smooth form of l.227 (what lem:surface_complete needs at l.1601)? Reading taken: the Lipschitz form Causal.Flat.IsCauchyComplete 2, so that (ii) => (i) and Step 1 compose; it makes the core's use of lem_surface_complete_two unavailable as formalized.
'M_1 the maximal BTZ-extension' (l.1596): read as any IsMaximal GHExt (OQ-150 (a)), so no RichardsInput is needed for Step 1.

kb_proposals: The Cauchy-maximal extension of a GH E0-manifold as a bundled E0Mfd with IsE0CauchyMaximal is GX.BTZCauchySpear.exists_cauchyMaximalExt (e0_cbg_isETTMaximal plus composition of Cauchy embeddings); reuse it rather than unpacking Causal.CBG.Dev.
The image of a Cauchy embedding of E0-manifolds is causally convex: GX.BTZCauchySpear.causallyConvexIn_range (causallyConvexIn_of_isCauchySurfaceOn with e0_sfa_of_globalBTZ and e0_curvesExtend).

BTZ-maximality as surjectivity: corestrict j : M1 -> M2 to an open Z with Z \ range j in sing_0, it is a BTZ-embedding (isE0Mor_corestrict_iff, mem_S0_iff_of_isE0Mor (isE0Mor_val Z)); a GH Z makes it an extMor and BTZMax.isInextensible_of_isMaximal makes it onto (spearInt_subset_range). Only GH of Z is the work.
